timeline_findings.finding: The 2026-02-25 Project-Frankenstein vision architecture already implemented an explicit cheap-first escalation topology: YOLO plus OCR and scene heuristics in Stage 1, with VLM escalation only when needed.
timeline_findings.current_mapping: Structural ancestor of the current fast-familiar-path/deep-perception split. Reuse the escalation principle, not its exact detectors or VLM backend.

timeline_findings.finding: The 2026-03-19 FrankEye consolidation deleted the earlier adaptive visual pipeline files and merged Digital Retina v8 CNN, DINOv2 INT8 ONNX scene features, OCR, faces and GoL-derived features into one CPU-oriented vision module.
timeline_findings.current_mapping: Provides a historical compact structured-feature surface suitable in principle as a frozen representation source, but the inspected module did not establish the current user-scoped prototype/classifier lifecycle.

timeline_findings.finding: The 2026-03-24 FrankEye correction explicitly removed CIFAR-10 classification from screenshots as useless while retaining screenshot-specific app/UI/OCR logic.
timeline_findings.current_mapping: Generic coarse object classes are a demonstrated poor proxy for user-specific visual familiarity. Do not use broad class labels as the MVC authority or primary familiarity signal.

timeline_findings.finding: At the frozen Project-Frankenstein head, tools/native_vision.py states that native Qwen3.5 multimodal vision replaces FrankEye entirely and removes CNN, DINOv2, ONNX and Tesseract from this path. The implementation base64-encodes an image, calls the multimodal model and returns natural-language output.
timeline_findings.current_mapping: Strong semantic deep-perception path, but by itself it does not expose the stable structured feature/prototype/version/replay surface required by the fixed FRANK 0.1 Micro Visual Classifier contract.

timeline_findings.finding: The Drive Digital Retina lineage and Project-Frankenstein lineage are complementary rather than redundant: Drive preserves explicit learned centroid/dictionary/replay and threshold-calibration mechanisms; Project-Frankenstein preserves production escalation, integration, simplification and eventual native multimodal semantic perception.
timeline_findings.current_mapping: Current FRANK 0.1 should preserve native multimodal semantic escalation while restoring only the minimal structured, versioned familiarity feature hook needed for MVC-0/MVC-1, rather than resurrecting FrankEye wholesale.

negative_results_and_constraints: Generic CIFAR-10 screenshot classification was explicitly removed as useless; it must not be mistaken for evidence of personal familiarity.

The current frozen-head native_vision.py produces model prose but does not itself persist per-user prototypes, trusted-example tiers, calibrated open-set state, candidate/current versions, rollback or deterministic replay receipts.
Native multimodal semantic recognition is not equivalent to calibrated user familiarity and must not bypass sensor evidence/provenance solely because the model can describe an image.

Reintroducing the entire historical FrankEye stack would add components whose current value is unproven; the fixed requirement is a minimal adaptive familiarity/routing layer, not restoration of a superseded vision architecture.

cross_source_reconciliation.drive_lineage: Historical Digital Retina provides learned prototype/centroid dictionary, cached replay and realistic-negative threshold/FPR evidence.
cross_source_reconciliation.project_frankenstein_lineage: Project-Frankenstein provides adaptive escalation, unified CPU perception, screenshot-specific failure correction and eventual native Qwen multimodal perception.
cross_source_reconciliation.dedup_rule: No duplicate earned-work credit is assigned. These lineages are mapped as distinct mechanism families with an integration dependency.
cross_source_reconciliation.converged_architecture_hypothesis: native Qwen semantic perception + stable frozen structured visual feature receipt + user-scoped MVC prototype/linear readout + calibrated open-set gate + bounded learner/replay/rollback

retain: Native Qwen multimodal perception as the deep semantic escalation path unless later measurements falsify it.
Cheap-first/deep-on-uncertainty routing inherited from the February adaptive pipeline.
Drive-derived prototype/centroid familiarity and frozen replay principles.
Explicit user-scope, GOLD/SILVER admission, open-set calibration, candidate shadow evaluation, rollback and versioning from the current fixed directive.
do_not_restore_by_default: Full FrankEye CNN+DINOv2+OCR+GoL stack as a monolithic service.
Prose-only model descriptions as classifier state or training truth.
current_architecture_delta.implementation_implication: H1 should add the smallest stable structured feature interface below or beside native semantic vision. MVC-0 uses versioned per-user centroids/prototypes over that frozen feature; MVC-1 may add a tiny linear head only if MVC-0 misses frozen acceptance thresholds.
current_architecture_delta.backbone_question: Compare a small reusable DINO/CLIP-like frozen embedding against any reproducibly accessible stable Qwen visual embedding. If the Qwen runtime cannot expose an embedding with stable version/replay semantics, reject it as the MVC backbone even if it is convenient for deep perception.
current_architecture_delta.recommended_discriminating_test: On H1 project hardware, compare (A) frozen compact external visual embedding + centroid MVC, (B) reproducibly exposed Qwen visual embedding + centroid MVC if available, and (C) native-Qwen-only no-MVC baseline on recurring user-specific classes plus realistic OOD/near-neighbor negatives. Preregister known-class accuracy, open-set AUROC/FPR at target recall, calibration, latency, CPU/RAM, routing savings, sequential retention, bounded update cost and crash/restart/replay behavior.
